items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2490

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to notice whenever a
sex offender is released to a public housing residence


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Provides notice to public housing authorities whenever a sex offender
is released to public housing.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Any state or local correctional facility, hospital or institution
where a sex offender was confined or committed shall provide notice to
public housing authorities whenever a sex offender is released to
public housing. The Division of Parole shall provide notice to public
housing authorities when a sex offender expects to reside in a public
housing dwelling.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Federal law prohibits convicted sex offenders from living in public
housing. NYC Council Member Eric Goia released a report revealing that
over 100 sex offenders were residing in NYCHA developments. DOCS and
the Division of Parole have an obligation to immediately inform public
housing authorities when a sex offender expects to reside in a public
housing development.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :;
2007-08 (A7442)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to the state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the 30th day after becoming law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2490A

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to notice whenever a
sex offender is released to a public housing residence


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Provides notice to public housing authorities whenever a sex offender
is released to public housing or has a change in address.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Any state or local correctional facility, hospital or institution
where a sex offender was confined or committed shall provide notice to
public housing authorities whenever a sex offender is discharged,
paroled, or released from any state or local correctional facility,
hospital or institution to public housing. Additionally, whenever a
sex offender reports a change of address to the sex offender registry
and said address is within a public housing authority dwelling, DCJS
shall forward the sex offender's information to such public housing
authority.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Federal law prohibits level 2 and 3 sex offenders from living in
public housing. NYC Council Member Eric Goia released a report
revealing that over 100 sex offenders were residing in NYCHA
developments. DOCS and the Division of Parole have an obligation to
immediately inform public housing authorities when a sex offender
expects to reside in a public housing development.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-08 (A7442)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to the state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the 30th day after becoming law.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S2490B

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the correction law, in relation to notice whenever a sex
offender is released to a public housing residence

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
Provides notice to public housing authorities whenever a level two or
level three sex offender is released to public housing or has a
change in address.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Any state or local correctional facility, hospital or institution
where a sex offender was confined or committed shall provide notice
to public housing authorities whenever a level two or level three sex
offender is discharged, paroled, or released from any state or local
correctional facility, hospital or institution to public housing.
Additionally, whenever a level two or level three sex offender
reports a change of address to the sex offender registry and said
address is within a public housing authority dwelling, DCJS shall
forward the sex offender's information to such public housing
authority.

JUSTIFICATION:
Federal law prohibits level 2 and 3 sex offenders from living in
public housing. NYC Council Member Eric Goia released a report
revealing that over 100 sex offenders were residing in NYCHA
developments. DOCS and the Division of Parole have an obligation to
immediately inform public housing authorities when a sex offender
expects to reside in a public housing development. Further, DCJS has
the same obligation whenever the sex offender registry is updated by
a level two or three sex offender, indicating public housing as an
address.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
2007-08 (A7442)

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the 30th day after becoming law.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2490C

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to notice whenever a
sex offender is released to a public housing residence

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Provides notice to public housing authorities whenever a level two or
level three sex offender is released to public housing or has a change
in address. Further corrects irregularities and grammatical mistakes
in the existing law.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Sections 1, 2 and 3 correct existing grammatical mistakes.

Section 4 amends §168-j of the correction law to require law
enforcement agencies to adhere to the notification provisions set
forth in subdivision 6 of §168-l of the correction law, whenever a sex
offender changes his/her address or status of enrollment, attendance,
employment or residence at an institution of higher education.

Section 5 amends §168-1 of the correction law to change the word "may"
to "shall," thereby eliminating any ambiguity in the current law as it
relates to law enforcement agencies' duty to inform vulnerable
organizations whenever a level two or level three sex offender is
convicted and moves into a particular neighborhood. In addition, "all
subsidized public housing projects" are added to the list of
vulnerable organizations that must be notified about the presence of
registered offenders.

Section 6 relates to the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 1998, Congress banned subsidized housing for the most serious sex
offenders after a convicted sex offender was charged with assaulting
and molesting a 9-year-old neighbor girl who lived in the same public
housing building. Also known as the Quality Housing and work
Responsibility Act, this new legislation prohibited housing
authorities from admitting any household that includes a person
subject to the lifetime sex offender registration requirement.

In March 2009, a report released by Councilman Eric Gioia found 126
sex offenders living in New York city public housing facilities, up
12% from the year before. 42 of the City's 3,432 registered sex
offenders live in projects in Brooklyn, 37 in Manhattan, 26 in the
Bronx, 8 in Queens and 3 in Staten Island.

More recently, a report by the Inspector General of the Housing and
Urban Development (HUD) Department, however, estimated that roughly
2,100-3,000 households currently residing in federally subsidized
housing include a serious sex offender. According to investigators,
the primary reason why HUD failed to meet the law's objective was that
HUD failed to ask prospective residents if they were subject to a
lifetime registration requirement and did not require housing
authorities to check the national sex offender registry prior to
recertifying the eligibility of its current residents.

This bill addresses the apparent lack of communication between local
law enforcement and public housing authorities by adding subsidized
public housing projects to the list of vulnerable organizations that
are notified whenever a level two or level three sex offender moves
into the community and changes his/her address or status of
enrollment, employment or attendance at an institution of higher
education.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-08: (A.7442)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
The HUD Inspector General estimates that more than $12 million could
be saved annually by not subsidizing housing for households with a
lifetime registered sex offender.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the 30th day after becoming law.

D.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2490D

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to notice whenever a
sex offender is released to a public housing residence


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Requires the Division of Criminal Justice Services to make its sex
offender registry information available to municipal housing
authorities at least once a month.  Further, upon request by such
municipal housing authority, the Division shall provide information
regarding a current or prospective tenant of the authority. The
information to be made available shall be the names of such offenders
whose address is within the same municipality or expected place of
domicile as the housing authority.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 1: Amends Correction Law section 168-b to provide that the
Division shall make available sex offender registry information to
municipal housing authorities to ensure that such persons do not live
in such public housing projects as is provided for under Federal Law.

Section 2: Amends Correction Law section §168-1 to add "municipal
housing authorities" to the list of "vulnerable organizations" that
needs to be notified about the presence of registered level two and
level three offenders.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 1998, Congress banned subsidized housing for the most serious sex
offenders after a convicted sex offender was charged with assaulting
and molesting a 9-year-old neighbor girl who lived in the same public
housing building. Also known as the Quality Housing and work
Responsibility Act, this new legislation prohibited housing
authorities from admitting any household that includes a person
subject to the lifetime sex offender registration requirement.

In March 2009, a report released by NYC Councilman Eric Gioia found
126 sex offenders living in New York city public housing facilities,
up 12% from the year before. 42 of the City's 3,432 registered sex
offenders live in projects in Brooklyn, 37 in Manhattan, 26 in the
Bronx, 8 in Queens and 3 in Staten Island.

More recently, a report by the Inspector General of the Housing and
Urban Development (HUD) Department, estimated that roughly 2,100-3,000
households currently residing in federally subsidized housing include
a serious sex offender. According to investigators, the primary reason
why HUD failed to meet the law's objective was that HUD failed to ask
prospective residents if they were subject to a lifetime registration
requirement and did not require housing authorities to check the
national sex offender registry prior to recertifying the eligibility
of its current residents.

This bill addresses the apparent lack of communication between local
law enforcement and public housing authorities by adding subsidized
public housing projects to the list of vulnerable organizations that
are notified whenever a level two or level three sex offender moves
into the community. The list is to be directly disseminated each month
to all municipal housing authorities. Further, the local municipal
housing authority may inquire of the Division about current or
prospective tenants.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-08: (A.7442)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
The HUD Inspector General estimates that more than $12 million could
be saved annually by not subsidizing housing for households with a
lifetime registered sex offender.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect 60 days after it shall have become law.
